issues.title: Discrete norm estimate quantifier
issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's explicit scalar/vector notation, the clauses 'for any v' do not quantify the bold vector bv occurring in the norms. Consequently the displayed universal estimates contain an unbound argument, even though H^1(Omega)^d and the surrounding formulas make the intended vector variable unambiguous.
issues.overall_effect: The trace estimate and its repeated proof display are formally malformed. Binding the actual vector argument restores the estimate used in the boundary and compactness arguments without changing its content.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each scalar quantifier “v ∈ H^1(Ω)^d” attached to a formula involving the bold vector v by the corresponding bold-vector quantifier, including est:trace-h and its repeated proof display. No downstream argument needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The paper’s explicit scalar/vector convention, the vector-valued space, and every displayed norm uniquely determine the bound variable. This is an unbound-symbol transcription error; correcting it changes no estimate, inference, or dependent guarantee.

issues.title: Scott--Zhang normal-trace space
issues.failure_explanation: H^1_n(Omega) is already defined using R^d-valued fields. Thus H^1_n(Omega)^d denotes a product of vector-field spaces, whereas PiSZ accepts one vector field and the proof acts on one vector field. The zero-normal-trace item is consequently ill-typed as written.
issues.overall_effect: The normal-trace-preservation item has an incompatible operator interface. The later Scott--Zhang test-function construction and the convergence results depending on it require the corrected single-vector-field space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the redundant outer power d from H^1_n(Ω)^d throughout itm:SZ-normal, so that the Scott–Zhang operator acts on the already vector-valued space H^1_n(Ω). Use that corrected type in its later test-function invocation.
issues.why_classification: H^1_n(Ω) is explicitly defined as a space of single vector fields, and both the operator domain and proof act on one such field. Deleting the duplicate vectorization is the uniquely forced typing correction and requires no mathematical repair.

issues.title: Continuous inf-sup test space
issues.failure_explanation: The old supremum quantifies a bold velocity variable over scalar H^1_0(Omega), yet its numerator applies the divergence operator to that variable. The internally consistent Stokes test space is H^1_0(Omega)^d, as also used by the discrete inf-sup assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The background continuous inf-sup assertion is ill-typed. The later analysis uses the separately and correctly stated discrete inf-sup assumption, so no formal-result dependency is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the supremum test space H^1_0(Ω) by H^1_0(Ω)^d in est:inf-sup-const, leaving the remainder of the inf-sup display unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The bold test variable, its divergence, and the correctly typed discrete inf-sup condition uniquely force the vector-valued Stokes test space. The omitted power d is purely transcriptional, and the display is not used by later results.

issues.title: Numerical convective bound
issues.failure_explanation: For fixed u and w, the form is linear in v. Whenever the form is nonzero, replacing v by t v scales the old left-hand side by |t| while leaving its right-hand side unchanged. The displayed right-hand side is instead the estimate obtained after setting v=u.
issues.overall_effect: The display falsely asserts a bound uniform in an arbitrary second argument. Subsequent formal results use only the valid diagonal expression with the first two arguments equal, so their conclusions do not depend on the overbroad part.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specialize the left-hand side of eq:traccovanish to |b̃(u,u,w)|, which gives exactly the displayed right-hand side by est:conv-a1. Retain the general bounded-trilinear conclusion using est:conv-a1 itself; no subsequent formal result requires an estimate uniform in an arbitrary second argument.
issues.why_classification: The arbitrary-v assertion is genuinely false by linear scaling and is not merely a well-typed universal estimate. One must either specialize to the diagonal case or restore the missing v-dependent factors. The diagonal repair is nevertheless short and routine, preserves every actual use and the general continuity conclusion, and causes no meaningful mathematical loss.

issues.title: Bulk norm in the trace estimate
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof claims to use the established L^2(I;H^1(Omega)) bound and the trace inequality, but writes an L^2(I;H^1(Gamma)) norm that is neither the bulk velocity space nor uniformly established. The trace theorem directly supplies the revised H^1(Omega) right-hand side.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, the proof does not establish its uniform trace bound and hence leaves a gap in the following boundary-stress and compactness chain. The corrected bulk norm supplies exactly the bound used downstream.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In est:unst-ap-11 replace the right-hand norm L^2(I;H^1(Γ)) by L^2(I;H^1(Ω)). Then apply the already stated bulk H^1 bound and trace inequality; no downstream estimate needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The preceding bulk estimate, the stated trace theorem, and the left-hand boundary norm uniquely force Ω on the right-hand side. The occurrence of Γ is a domain-label transcription error rather than a missing estimate or lemma, so the entire affected chain is restored by that correction.

issues.title: Dual exponent in stress convergence
issues.failure_explanation: Coercivity bounds the regularized stress in L^{r'}, and eq:conv-unst-6c2 correctly extracts its weak-star limit there. The subsequent assertion of weak-star convergence in L^r is unsupported and is false in the relevant r>2 regime, where r'<r. The limit identity for sigma must use the established dual-exponent convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The proof's stated basis for identifying sigma as the regularized-stress limit minus lambda times the trace uses the wrong function space. Correcting the exponent restores that relation and the implicit-boundary identification chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted weak-star convergence of the regularized stress in L^r(I;L^r(Γ)^d) by convergence in L^{r′}(I;L^{r′}(Γ)^d), consistently with est:unst-ap-13 and eq:conv-unst-6c2, and use that convergence when passing to σ = σ̂ − λ tr_τ(u).
issues.why_classification: The conjugate exponent r′ is already established explicitly immediately before the erroneous assertion and is uniquely forced by coercivity. Correcting the copied exponent preserves the same limit identity and every dependent theorem without any new argument or weakened guarantee.

issues.title: Pressure limit test derivative
issues.failure_explanation: lem:unst-conv-pi states that the time-integrated pressure converges against -partial_t phi, and eq:pressure-1 proves exactly that formula. Therefore the old limit in eq:unst-lim-4 with an undifferentiated phi does not follow and cannot establish the proposition's displayed full distributional equation, which itself contains partial_t phi.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not justify its asserted pressure term for general, non-divergence-free test fields. The pressure-free formulation used by the main convergence theorems is unaffected because the pressure term vanishes for divergence-free tests.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct eq:unst-lim-4 to state that ∫⟨π^k,div v_h⟩φ^k dt converges to −∫⟨ξ,div v⟩∂_tφ dt. With the preceding minus sign in the discrete equation, this yields the pressure term in eq:unst-lim-eq-1a.
issues.why_classification: The pressure-convergence lemma, its integration-by-parts identity, and the proposition’s target distributional equation all uniquely require ∂_tφ. The omitted derivative is a transcriptional omission; inserting it repairs no underlying inference and leaves the pressure-free conclusions unchanged.

issues.title: r>2 identification lemma range
issues.failure_explanation: The lemma's prose claims the conditions of thm:main-unsteady, which restrict r to [1,2] and concern the earlier regime. Its proof and surrounding section instead use r>2 and the antisymmetric scheme governed by thm:main-unsteady-v. Thus the argument supports a different hypothesis set from the one literally stated.
issues.overall_effect: The identification lemma does not formally supply the r>2 premise used to conclude the antisymmetric convergence theorem until its governing hypotheses are corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reference to the conditions of thm:main-unsteady by the conditions of thm:main-unsteady-v, equivalently stating the implicit-relation, antisymmetric-scheme regime r ∈ (2,2^♯). The lemma’s proof and conclusion then apply unchanged and supply thm:main-unsteady-v.
issues.why_classification: The r>2 section heading, the immediately preceding antisymmetric theorem, the proof’s opening assumption r>2, and the recorded dependent theorem uniquely force the corrected cross-reference. This is a wrong-label transcription error, not a new hypothesis analysis or proof repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: It suffices to consider the case $r>2$.
